children: , the cloud-native cybersecurity provider, received a Needham price-target increase to $310 from $250 as its Flex subscription model drew fresh attention. Shares rose approximately 2.6% to $269.82 around 12:02 p.m. ET Friday, Oct. 9. That leaves roughly 15% upside to the new target. The bullish case hinges on getting customers to buy more security products through a single spending commitment.

According to Stocktwits' reporting, Needham estimates that initial Flex migrations lift annual recurring revenue by an average of about 40%. That is an analyst estimate, rather than a company-disclosed cohort figure. CrowdStrike's second-quarter results provide firmer evidence of growth: annual recurring revenue climbed 25% to $5.84 billion, while subscription revenue increased 27% to $1.40 billion. Flex could help customers expand across the platform without negotiating every module separately.

The valuation picture raises the bar: shares sit 95.3% above the displayed GF Value estimate of $138.16. That premium signals substantial growth expectations, rather than proving the stock must fall. Bigger contracts are a promising start. The harder test is turning those commitments into lasting usage and renewals while protecting margins. Investors need to watch whether Flex delivers that growth without leaning too heavily on discounts.

title: CrowdStrike Stocks Gain 2.6% as Needham Lifts Target 24%
